purpose: Teach: こもり/思いがけない/片づけ/寝かせ/横顔/思い当たる/ホタル/育た

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さん、書斎にこもりがちだったぞ
lines.en: When you were young, your father used to shut himself away in his study.
lines.style: Distant, reflective voice. Slow measured pace. Gazing backward through time. A small smile lives in the words, not the delivery.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃんから思いがけないお花、頂いたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and your grandfather surprised me with flowers sometimes, didn't he?
lines.style: Warm, conversational. A soft affection underneath. She's building on his memory gently, adding her own thread. Knowing and tender without being sentimental.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お祖父ちゃん、書類の片づけお得意だったぞ
lines.en: When you were young, your grandfather was quite good at keeping his papers in order.
lines.style: Still gazing backward. A quieter observation this time. The pace remains measured. There's something like admiration woven through it—for a small, steady habit.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫さんを寝かせるのお上手だったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather had such a gift for putting the grandchildren to sleep, didn't he?
lines.style: Appreciative, almost sing-song in its gentleness. A memory surfacing that makes her voice soften further. She's offering him the thing he's looking for—recognition of love shown in small ways.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、ばあさんの横顔、お父さん見惚れたぞ
lines.en: When you were young, your father used to gaze at your mother's profile.
lines.style: Voice becomes quieter, more tender. The words arrive slowly. There's something vulnerable in admitting he noticed love. A slight catch on 'profile,' like the image still moves him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お父さんに思い当たる癖、ありますわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your grandfather had some of your father's habits, didn't he? Certain little quirks?
lines.style: Knowing, almost delighted. She's seen the pattern across generations and wants him to see it too. Warm curiosity in the delivery. Slight emphasis on 'habits'—like she's connecting invisible threads.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、田んぼでホタルを見たぞ
lines.en: When you were young, you saw fireflies in the rice paddies.
lines.style: Voice softens to almost a whisper. The image is crystalline in his memory. Slow, reverent pace. He's offering something precious—a moment of pure beauty he's carried all this time.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 日陰の場所では育たない苗もあったぞ、覚えてる。お祖父ちゃんに育てられたお花、立派でしたわね、あなた?
lines.en: Some seedlings won't grow in the shade, you remember. Your grandfather tended his flowers beautifully—they grew so strong, didn't they?
lines.style: Tender, knowing. She's not just remembering with him—she's translating his memory. Metaphorical, gentle. The words arrive with quiet care, like she's helping him see what his father was doing all along.
